current_episode.title: 119. Celebrating 15 Years of Ariel Property Advisors in CRE with Shimon Shkury & Roxanne Donovan

guest.bio_context: Shkury started his career in 2002 at Massey Knuckle Realty, where he became a partner two years later before co-founding Ariel Property Advisors on January 10, 2011, alongside Victor Sozio, Ivan Petrovich, and Mike Tortorici. He built expertise in Upper Manhattan and the Bronx market intelligence, which became the foundation for Ariel's information-first advisory model across New York City's commercial real estate sectors including affordable housing, rent-stabilized housing, development, and capital markets.

context.transcript_excerpt: Good morning and welcome to the Coffee and Cap Rates podcast, your go-to source for New York City's latest commercial real estate insights. This program is brought to you by Ariel Property Advisors. So I'm so happy to be here today. Thanks for letting me talk to you about this exciting milestone for Ariel Property Advisors. Thank you so much, Roxanne. I'm excited to be here with you and we share swimming, so I love that about you. So we'll just swim right in. Yes, let's do it. So congratulations on the 15th anniversary of the company. Can you tell me a little bit about the – what's the origin story? Where does Ariel Property Advisors come from? Yeah, so it's a super exciting story. I started my career in 2002, and I started it at a company that everybody knows called Massey Knuckle Realty, and two years later became a partner in that company and helped build it. But what was more interesting to me personally is that I managed to meet some incredible people. I managed to meet Victor Sozio who started with me back at Massey and today is a founding partner at Ariel. Ivan Petrovich was also a founding partner at Ariel and started with me back at Massey. And Mike Tortorici who is also a founding partner at Ariel. All of us grew within that great system, organized system. And one of the things we did is to make sure that the information we have at the time for Upper Manhattan and the Bronx is the best information that there is in the industry. If you remember the early 2000s, there wasn't a lot of information, right? No. If you weren't in Midtown, you were off the map, really. Here you go. And so if you were focusing on information in Upper Manhattan, the Bronx, you were pretty much the number one broker, advisor, information agent for that area. And we felt within time that we can do more than just Upper Manhattan, the Bronx, which was our territory. and we felt that we can centralize the company around that information and take it to the next level citywide. That's exactly what we did in January 10th of 2011, which was a great day for us to start and was right after the global financial crisis. We started recovering from that. And I remember these few days going with all of my partners into a new office space and starting it out and trying to get listings and so on. And here we are today, 65 people after seven partners. So it's exciting. It is exciting. Are there some milestones over those 15 years that you're especially proud of or highlights from this time that you look back on and say that was a turning point? I think that for us, it's the people that we got in, right? It's all about the people. So Vic, Mike, Yvonne and myself clearly are the founding partners. But then we had Paul McCormick join us back in about 2014 or so. And his role was to build capital services, so start a business line for us. And he did that so well that now he manages all of our salespeople and he's a partner in the company. The second person that came in and became a partner is Sean Kelly. He's done tremendously well in Brooklyn and over time became a partner as well. And the third partner is Aviva Viad, who is our CFO. And so all of these people are leaders in the company in addition to, again, Vic, Mike, Ivan and myself. And that is the basis to every growth we have. We have some senior directors. We have some directors that we're very proud of. And so when I look at milestones, it's about the people and it's about what will be built in terms of career progression. And so we have a career progression that says you come in as an associate. Here's how you can become a partner in the company. Here's how you can own a piece of the company. And so these are the milestones that I see are super important. And then it's clearly about the clientele that grew with us. It's about the focus. It's about the different verticals. It's about affordable housing, understanding rent-stabilized housing, understanding development, understanding faith-based organizations

pending_qa.q: What role do live events play in thought leadership and community engagement for a commercial real estate platform?
pending_qa.r: Coffee and Cap Rates is held twice a year in February and July, bringing together 30 market reports, quick market analysis, and industry players for discussion. The event has grown from 50 attendees to over 300 people, with 100% of proceeds plus matching funds going to Legal Outreach nonprofit, partnering with TD Bank. The event serves as a culmination of information and thought leadership while supporting nonprofit mission work and empowering clients and communities.

pending_qa.q: How can a commercial real estate firm build company culture around social leadership and community involvement?
pending_qa.r: Ariel Property Advisors calls this local leadership and discusses it every Monday morning, making nonprofit or professional organization involvement part of each team member's business plan. The founding partners model this by sitting on boards and attending events: Shkury serves on Israeli bonds and FIDF boards, Mike Tortorici works with Inner City for Catholic Kids, Victor Sozio sits on NYSAFA's board, and Sean Kelly organizes charity golf outings. All team members, junior and senior, participate and match their charitable giving, making it core to company culture.

pending_qa.q: What are the core values and operational practices that enable a real estate firm to rank among the best companies to work for nationally?
pending_qa.r: Globe Street ranked Ariel as one of the best commercial real estate companies to work for, driven by their mission-based core values centered on one team, accountability, commitment, personal growth, and innovation. Shkury emphasizes working on culture daily by bringing teams together to resolve friction, creating a nurturing environment, and breaking silos by opening their Salesforce database so everyone sees everyone's work. They target two to five-year professionals who feel stalled elsewhere, offering 65 people supporting each individual's growth with internal encouragement rather than internal competition.

pending_qa.q: How should a commercial real estate advisory firm evaluate multi-year performance and respond during market downturns?
pending_qa.r: Rather than looking at single-year performance, Shkury advises examining the past three years: 2022 was good, but 2023 and 2024 were tough due to rising interest rates that stopped transactions. During downturns, the strategy is to talk to clients, advise them, hold their hand, and think through possibilities together. By 2025, when markets opened and Mayor Adams implemented City of Yes, 485X, and 467M for office conversions, Ariel was positioned to capture opportunities because relationships had been developed and maintained during the difficult period.

pending_qa.q: What specific market sectors and deal types drove commercial real estate transaction growth in 2025?
pending_qa.r: Development sites waiting for housing policy benefited from Mayor Adams' rezoning initiatives including City of Yes and 485X for conversion, plus 467M for office conversions. Capital services growth accelerated with new deal types including office conversion financing and hotel financing. Affordable housing, rent-stabilized, and faith-based organizations saw significant growth, including an $88 million deal sold to Treadway with Related as client. A strategic alliance with Global Real Estate Advisors started bearing fruit in both capital services and affordable housing.

pending_qa.q: What is the structure and value proposition of Global Real Estate Advisors partnership for a local boutique firm?
pending_qa.r: Global Real Estate Advisors (GREA) operates six offices covering about 12 markets, with Ariel Property Advisors doing every product type while other offices focus mostly on multifamily. Ariel stays independent and autonomous while plugging into the national platform. The partnership creates value through debt and equity placement services shared across offices, national affordable housing expertise with Victor Sozio heading that effort, national accounts coordination, and Ariel's overseas operations advantage in Belgrade where 25 people are fully integrated into operations, providing best practices to the platform.

pending_qa.q: What market dynamics are driving Class A office demand and rent growth in major business districts?
pending_qa.r: Class A and Class A plus office transactions grew 25% year over year, with Class A average rent reaching about $85 per square foot and Class A plus above $100. A building on 57th Street is asking more than $300 per square foot for office penthouse space. There is significant demand and depth for premium office space with insufficient supply, which also drives competition in Class B office, making it harder to find available space than a year prior.

pending_qa.q: What regulatory and policy reforms are needed to address the affordable housing crisis in New York City?
pending_qa.r: Shkury argues that HSTPA needs reform or removal, requiring city and state to work together on whether to help landlords convert buildings to affordable housing, provide subsidies and tax breaks, create pathways to profitability for affordable housing, or provide private incentives for reinvestment. Without intervention, rent-stabilized buildings risk deterioration. Mayor Adams and Governor Hochul made progress with zoning changes, but more action is needed to increase housing supply and lower rents through production rather than regulation alone.

pending_qa.q: Which international and domestic investor groups are currently seeking real estate opportunities in New York City?
pending_qa.r: Japanese investors have returned to the market, alongside investors from Israel, Germany, and various sovereign wealth funds and family offices seeking entry into New York City. They operate through different models: establishing local operations and buying directly, bringing equity through local partners, or investing through known entities like purchasing portions of major buildings. National investors also see opportunity in New York City because cap rates are higher there compared to Sunbelt markets, which are oversupplied and have lower demand.
